Pahathmoab
pā´hath-mō´ab
n. (head of one of the largest families to return from Babylon)
Hebrew Pachath Moab, literally governor of Moab — a title turned into a family name, probably from an ancestor who had held office in that territory.

Biblical Definition

The family is among the largest in the register of the return: “The children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve” (Ezra 2:6). A second company came up with Ezra himself years later: “Of the sons of Pahathmoab; Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males” (Ezra 8:4). But the same house appears in the painful list of those who had taken foreign wives: “And of the sons of Pahathmoab; Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh” (Ezra 10:30). And the house is on the wall in Nehemiah's day: “Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hashub the son of Pahathmoab, repaired the other piece, and the tower of the furnaces” (Nehemiah 3:11). Three thousand people, a repaired tower, and a column of names under discipline — the record of one family across two generations, kept without flattery and without concealment.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Pahath-moab; the Hebrew signifies governor of Moab, and the name heads a large family of the return.

PAHATH-MOAB, n. The head of a great family among the returning exiles; in Hebrew, governor of Moab.

EXILE, n. The state of being banished from one's country; the person banished.

RETURN, n. The act of coming back to the same place or state; restoration.

DISCIPLINE, n. Correction; chastisement; punishment intended to correct crimes or errors.

TOWER, n. A building, either round or square, raised to a considerable elevation, for defence or ornament.

Key Scripture

Ezra 2:6 — "The children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve ."

Ezra 8:4 — "Of the sons of Pahathmoab; Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males."

Ezra 10:30 — "And of the sons of Pahathmoab; Adna, and Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezaleel, and Binnui, and Manasseh."

Nehemiah 3:11 — "Malchijah the son of Harim, and Hashub the son of Pahathmoab, repaired the other piece, and the tower of the furnaces."

Modern Corruption

Church discipline is treated as incompatible with grace, though Ezra names the offending households of the returned community and records the correction rather than suppressing it.

expand to see more

Ezra 10 is a chapter modern readers find intolerable, and the difficulty deserves a straight answer rather than an evasion. The issue was not ethnicity; Ruth the Moabitess and Rahab the Canaanite are in the line of Christ, and the law provided for the stranger who joined himself to the LORD. The issue was the covenant, and specifically marriages contracted with the surrounding peoples in their idolatry, which was the very sin that had destroyed the northern kingdom and sent Judah to Babylon. The community had come home under a covenant and the households named had broken it.

The name itself faces no postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Scripture records the failures of its best families without erasing their honours. The house of Pahath-moab returned nearly three thousand strong, sent another two hundred men with Ezra, and repaired the tower of the furnaces on the wall — and eight of its sons are listed by name among those who had to put away what they had taken. The same register holds both. A church willing to publish only one half of that account will end with neither honest discipline nor honest praise.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Pachath Moab (H6355), governor of Moab; golah (H1473), the exile or captivity; chazaq (H2388), to repair; nashim nokriyoth, strange wives.

expand to see more

Hebrew Pachath Moab (H6355) — governor of Moab; a family name of the return.

Hebrew pachah (H6346) — a governor, prefect; the office behind the name.

Hebrew golah (H1473) — the exiles, the captivity; the community being numbered.

Hebrew chazaq (H2388) — to repair, strengthen; Nehemiah 3:11, the tower of the furnaces.

Hebrew nokri (H5237) — foreign, strange; the wives put away in Ezra 10.

Usage

"“The children of Pahathmoab…two thousand eight hundred and twelve” — a great house."

"“Of the sons of Pahathmoab…two hundred males” — a second company with Ezra."

"“Hashub the son of Pahathmoab…the tower of the furnaces” — the same house on the wall."
